rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter is certain and follows necessarily from God's attributes; those with knowledge recognize it as reality.
rows.anchor: The Hereafter is an incontestable reality and the obvious corollary of God’s attributes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mockery of monotheism and the Hereafter comes from negligence, indifference, and loss of repentance and willingness to learn.
rows.anchor: Their real ailment is that they have become devoid of the traits of repentance and seeking a lesson.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can seize people whenever and wherever He wills, so they should learn from the warning.
rows.anchor: God can seize them whenever He wants and wherever He wants.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and Solomon received worldly favors without arrogance, remaining grateful and obedient; they made devils follow them rather than serving devils.
rows.anchor: God granted them with all the favours of this world but they never became arrogant and haughty and remained grateful and obedient to Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subordinates devils to those who follow Him, while devils overcome the ungrateful and make them their servants.
rows.anchor: God makes the devils become subservient to those who follow their Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Sheba exemplify nations that answer divine favors with arrogance and disorder, then face exemplary punishment and lose those favors.
rows.anchor: nations who after being bestowed with God’s favours become arrogant and spread anarchy in the land instead of becoming grateful are punished by God in an exemplary manner.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Sheba fulfilled Satan's prediction and were deprived of God's favors, becoming a tale of the ancients.
rows.anchor: The people of Sabā’ fulfilled the prediction of Satan about them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage refutes polytheism and intercession and tells the Prophet to leave stubborn idolaters' fate to God after fulfilling his duty.
rows.anchor: polytheism and intercession are refuted

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers opponents who demand to see the threatened punishment before they will believe in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: not willing to believe in the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affluent reject the Qur'an because they mistake worldly wealth and status for proof of divine favor and assume it guarantees success in the next life.
rows.anchor: they regarded themselves to be favoured ones of God because of the affluence and status they possessed in this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly favors test whether people are grateful; in the Hereafter each person is judged by deeds.
rows.anchor: God gives the favours of this world to people to test and try them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Hereafter God deals with each person according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: In the Hereafter, God will deal with a person on the basis of his deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels worshipped as deities will disclaim the idolaters and say that the idolaters were actually worshipping jinn.
rows.anchor: the angels will reply that they have in fact been worshipping the jinn and they themselves renounce having any relationship with the Idolaters.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding passage recalls the Qur'an as a great favor to people without prior scripture and urges serious reflection before deciding.
rows.anchor: attention is first directed at the great favour done by God to these people in the form of the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who let the opportunity pass will regret it forever and receive no further chance.
rows.anchor: they will regret forever but they will not be afforded any other opportunity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz denotes God's invincible dominance and al-Ḥakīm His wise action; their perfect realization leaves no room for partners.
rows.anchor: the attribute ُزیِزَعْال shows that He is inaccessible, dominant and powerful; the attribute ُمیِكَحْال implies that all actions of God are based on great wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A partner needed to create or govern would negate God's might, while one who could sway His justice would negate His wisdom; these are the idolaters' two misconceptions.
rows.anchor: both these misconceptions were the real cause of the polytheism of the Idolaters.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following passage answers opponents' objections and demands, then points to the inevitable fate of those denying truth through doubts.
rows.anchor: The succeeding verses deal with the objections

none: Qur’anic verses and their translation only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse laments people demanding the promised doom to reject the Qur'an's monotheism and warnings, and says they do so to harass the Prophet.
rows.anchor: This verse expresses sorrow at people who in order to reject the message of monotheism of the Qur’ān and its warnings about the punishments of the Herein and the Hereafter would demand that they be shown the promised doom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet brings glad tidings of mercy to believers who do good and warns rejecters of God's wrath; his duty ends with delivering the message, while God decides whether and when to punish.
rows.anchor: The Prophet’s responsibility ends after he delivers these glad tidings and warnings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that most people do not know expresses sorrow: a messenger gives people a chance to gain mercy, yet they demand punishment instead.
rows.anchor: such is the misfortune of people that they demand punishment instead of mercy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger's warning conclusively communicates truth; rejection then brings destruction under God's established practice.
rows.anchor: when the Almighty sends His messenger to a people, then the truth is conclusively communicated to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next sūrah confirms that every community received a warner, earlier messengers were rejected despite clear signs and scripture, and God seized the rejecters.
rows.anchor: Their messengers came to them with veritable signs, with scriptures, and with a radiant Book. Then I seized these people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers warned their own peoples, whereas Muhammad, the final messenger, was sent to all humanity; Qur'anic styles and earlier-scripture prophecies attest this.
rows.anchor: since Muh@ammad (sws) is the last of the prophets and messengers, he was sent towards all mankind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These words remind the People of the Book, who were supporting Quraysh, that Muhammad's message also determines their fate and they should consider the consequences.
rows.anchor: the messenger they are opposing in such a vehement manner is not merely a deliverer of glad tidings and warnings to the Quraysh; he will also decide the fate of the People of the Book.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of heeding the warning, opponents mock the Messenger and companions by asking sarcastically when the threat will arrive; unless shown or given its date, they call it a bluff.
rows.anchor: they try to belittle the messenger and his companions.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says rejecters stubbornly refuse the Qur'an and the punishment and Day of Judgement it announces unless these realities are shown to them.
rows.anchor: very stubbornly reply to the warnings of the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term wrongdoers refers to the unfortunate rejecters who disregarded God's mercy and demanded to see the punishment.
rows.anchor: these very unfortunate people who while disregarding God’s mercy were demanding to see His punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaders and followers are united in opposing the Qur'an now, although they will later dispute over responsibility.
rows.anchor: today their leaders and followers are united on opposing the message of the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: some interpreters
rows.claim: One interpretation takes what is ahead of the Qur'an to mean the books revealed before it.
rows.anchor: in two ways: one opinion is

rows.speaker: some interpreters
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes what is ahead of the Qur'an to mean the punishment and Day of Judgement it foretells.
rows.anchor: the second opinion is that this refers to the divine punishment and Day of Judgement about which the Qur’ān is informing people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi prefers the second interpretation in context: rejecters will not accept the Qur'an or the punishment and Resurrection it announces unless shown these realities.
rows.anchor: In my view, the second opinion is more consistent with the context.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional phrase about seeing wrongdoers before their Lord has an omitted conclusion because the scene is beyond depiction; its horror is left unsaid.
rows.anchor: The answer to the conditional clause is suppressed here as per linguistic principles.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who spurned mercy and demanded punishment; the omitted consequence of seeing them before God is too horrific to express.
rows.anchor: what is suppressed after “then” is so horrific that it cannot be expressed in words.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that they turn words back and forth means they will argue; although leaders and followers unite against the Qur'an now, each will blame the other at judgement.
rows.anchor: The words ُعِجْرَی ْمُهُضْعَب ىَلِإِ ٍضْعَب َلْوَقْال mean that they will argue and dispute with one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders lead the opposition while their followers vehemently follow them, though the two groups will later blame each other.
rows.anchor: the leaders are leading the way in this opposition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers vehemently follow their leaders in opposing the Qur'an, even though they will later try to blame them.
rows.anchor: the followers are vehemently following them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At judgement followers blame leaders for misleading them, while leaders say followers chose to follow; each learns it is accountable and cannot shift another's burden.
rows.anchor: each group will know that it is responsible for what it had done; no one will bear the burden of the other.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak masses blame wealthy leaders for their fate and say they would have believed absent pressure, even though truth was known and they wanted faith.
rows.anchor: the poor and the masses will blame their wealthy leaders

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oppressed say the truth was known and they wanted to accept it, but persistent pressure from leaders subdued them.
rows.anchor: the truth was not hidden from them and they also wanted to adopt it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders say they might accept some blame if guidance had not reached the masses, but since people stumbled in broad daylight they should blame themselves.
rows.anchor: they were ready to accept the blame to some extent

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking truth is everyone's responsibility, and once truth is evident each must follow it as far as possible; no one is excused without making that effort.
rows.anchor: the quest for the truth is everyone’s responsibility and once it becomes evident, it is his obligation to adhere to it as far as is possible for him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oppressed answer that leaders' day-and-night conspiracies and propaganda taught them to disbelieve in God and associate partners with Him.
rows.anchor: day and night conspiracies of the leaders

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase for concealing regret describes shame in the heart when torment appears; this signals their excuse will fail and conscience compounds their agony.
rows.anchor: when after this question and answer they see the torment of God hovering over them, they will feel very ashamed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their shame comes from recognizing they followed leaders against conscience; the consequences of evil choices bring both torment and remorse.
rows.anchor: against the calls of their conscience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The neck-yokes resemble the consequence of the disbelievers' choice to lull conscience and hand their reins to others; Hell's guards will drag them by them.
rows.anchor: lulling their intellect and conscience to sleep

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chains are no injustice: they manifest former deeds, since those who wore the yokes of servitude to people become chained in Hell.
rows.anchor: the yolks that will be put around the necks of the disbelievers will not constitute any injustice to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is reassured that affluent contemporaries repeat the arrogant rejection used by wealthy opponents of earlier messengers against monotheism and punishment warnings.
rows.anchor: whatever the affluent and rich people of his times are doing to him is nothing new.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “sent with” hints that, in the affluent opponents' eyes, the Prophet's claim to messengerhood has no basis.
rows.anchor: the messengerhood claimed by him is merely a claim which has no basis in their eyes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Affluent rejecters imagine that true messengers would have more wealth and children than they do.
rows.anchor: these messengers should have been far wealthier

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They infer from their prosperity that neither worldly nor afterlife punishment will reach them, treating affluence as a contradiction of the promised doom.
rows.anchor: neither be punished in this world nor in the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children neither prove divine favor nor unworthiness; God expands or constricts provision with wisdom, testing gratitude or patience, and true success appears in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: this abundance and paucity is based on God’s authority and wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic word ḍiʿf should not be read as meaning only a double reward.
rows.anchor: should not be construed as two times or double reward.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without faith and righteous deeds, wealth and children only increase a person's ruin.
rows.anchor: In the absence of faith and righteous deeds, wealth and children will only add to the ruin of such people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly wealth and children are exposed to danger, and people cannot protect themselves from those risks.
rows.anchor: in this world danger lurks everywhere for one’s wealth and children

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍiʿf can mean equal in amount or many multiples without a fixed limit; the faithful receive manifold reward, not necessarily only double.
rows.anchor: as well as many times the magnitude of a thing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chambers promise enduring safety and reward, unlike worldly wealth and children exposed to danger; the faithful need not fear loss in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: in this world danger lurks everywhere for one’s wealth and children and no one can protect oneself from these dangers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who use their wealth and children to oppose revelations and harass the Messenger will be seized and dragged into punishment; the wording conveys helpless humiliation.
rows.anchor: The word َونُرَضْحُم depicts their state of humiliation and helplessness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated opening about provision has different force: verse 36 stresses God's control and the test of gratitude or patience, so people should neither boast nor despair.
rows.anchor: Verse 36 explains that the abundance in sustenance and their scarcity is totally in the hands of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 39 tells the affluent to spend God's blessings on what pleases Him; no amount spent in His way is wasted, and He repays it.
rows.anchor: they will be rewarded for the smallest of amounts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “in God's way” is omitted after “whatever you spend” because context supplies it; “God replaces for you” means He returns what was lost.
rows.anchor: The words ْيِف ِلْیِبَس اللّٰہ are suppressed after اَمَو مُتْقَنفَأُ because of contextual indications.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best provider assures spenders that their small gifts will receive a recompense they cannot yet imagine; “best” states an attribute rather than comparison.
rows.anchor: The word ُرْیَخ better) here is not meant to express comparison with something.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next section warns wealthy idolaters that angels will disavow them, no one can save them, and they should learn from stronger nations whom God seized without refuge.
rows.anchor: the angels will declare their acquittal from them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Judgement is clearly attested; false deities cannot bring anyone near God, while pure monotheistic words gain acclaim through good deeds, making faith and righteous action the path to honor.
rows.anchor: these words receive acclaim through good deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth, children, and lifespan are God's gifts and control; cosmic harmony shows that an all-powerful sustaining God governs, while other deities can neither govern nor help at judgement.
rows.anchor: The harmony found in the conflicting elements of this universe clearly shows that it is being governed by the all-powerful and sustaining God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignoring the truth harms people rather than God, who does not need them; the Prophet's preaching reaches living hearts, while the dead-hearted face their ordained fate.
rows.anchor: God does not need them; it is they who need Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conflict between belief and disbelief, like the creation of light and darkness, serves divine wisdom; only people with knowledge and cognizance value these blessings and accept faith.
rows.anchor: this clash between belief and disbelief is also based on God’s wisdom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group among the People of the Book is praised for adhering to the Torah amid disorder and is expected to accept the Qur'an, which accords with predictions in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ān has come in accordance with the predictions about it found in the Torah and other scriptures.
